title: Bin El Ouidane reservoir, 4 Jul to 20 Oct 2026
summary: Between 4 Jul and 20 Oct 2026 the lake went from 31.86 km2 to 28.52 km2, while the whole circle got brighter, with mean HH up 1.79 dB. The 20 Oct date carries a flag, so the brightening should not be read as change on the ground.

sections.heading: What changed
sections.text: Over 108 days the lake changed by -3.34 km2, or -10.5%. HH turned brighter by more than 3 dB on 44.11 km2 and darker on only 0.12 km2. HV turned brighter on 11.46 km2, and mean HV rose by 0.83 dB.

sections.heading: Where, by terrain type
sections.text: The brightening covers every type. Rough dry ground and fields had 21.5 km2 brighter in HH and rose 2.72 dB, and trees, shrub and rugged slopes had 13.73 km2 brighter. Built-up land, which should stay stable, rose 2.68 dB in HH.

sections.heading: Possible causes
sections.text: Possible cause: a processing offset in the 20 Oct product, since buildings brightened like fields; reprocessed files would settle it. Possible cause: a wet surface after rain; rain records for October would check it. Possible cause for the lake: summer drawdown; the dam's level records would confirm it.

sections.heading: Limits
sections.text: 20 Oct 2026 carries a flag: backscatter over built-up land shifted more than 0.5 dB from its June-September median. NASA has no NISAR data from 27 Jul to 10 Aug 2026, so nothing between 16 Jul and 21 Aug 2026 is seen. Lake areas are approximate: 12.7% and 8.2% of the outline falls on land in the optical photo.

sections.heading: What an agency could do next
sections.text: Use an unflagged end date for a firm lake figure, and check October rain records before reading any land change here.
